metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent

brief.text:
The clearest piece of news today is in crude. Brent, the global benchmark crude grade, is at $93.07 a barrel, up $1.67 or 1.8% today, with WTI, the US benchmark, at $82.98, up 1.1%. One likely factor is the headline that Riyadh, the Houthi-controlled Yemeni port of Hodeidah and Ras Tanura — a major Saudi crude loading terminal — were hit in a Saudi-Houthi exchange of fire. For anyone fixing ships, strikes on or near export terminals matter twice over: they affect how much cargo is available to lift, and they feed war-risk insurance costs on Arabian Gulf and Red Sea voyages.

Bunker fuel moved the other way. VLSFO — very low sulphur fuel oil, the main compliant marine fuel — fell today at every hub: Rotterdam down $28.50 to $673.50 a tonne (-4.1%), Singapore down $21.50 to $833.50 (-2.5%), Fujairah down $15.00 to $787.00 and Houston down $12.00 to $708.00. Bunkers falling while crude rises is unusual and the data here does not show why. The two listed shipping ETFs both eased today, the tanker fund BWET down 1.2% to $808.92 and the dry bulk fund BDRY down 0.5% to $12.59. No Baltic freight index refreshed today: the Baltic Dry Index stood at 3,068 points on Tuesday, up 68, while the Capesize index — Capesizes are the largest dry bulk ships, typically iron ore and coal — was 4,779 on Monday, with Panamax at 2,149 and Supramax at 1,809 the same day. Tanker TCEs (time charter equivalent, daily earnings after voyage costs) are three sessions old: VLCC AG-China was $1,079,794 a day on Sunday, Suezmax $165,677 and MR Rotterdam-NY just $11,300.

Running stories: the Saudi-Houthi exchange is new today. The Libya strike story developed, with Ukraine denying interference after the Benghazi drone attack on Russian warships. Hormuz attacks, Black Sea strikes, Russian refinery damage and shadow-fleet sanctions had no fresh news in today's data and are unchanged. MEPC85, the IMO environment meeting that opens on 30 November without settled LNG carbon accounting, is also unchanged, though two LNG carrier orders from Bonny Gas Transport were reported.

Watch two things. First, whether Baltic indices refresh and how they sit against Monday and Tuesday's levels. Second, any further reporting on Ras Tanura, since terminal damage would bear directly on Arabian Gulf tanker demand and war-risk cover.

storylines.title: Saudi-Houthi strikes hit energy and port infrastructure
storylines.what: Riyadh, the Houthi-controlled port of Hodeidah and the Saudi terminal at Ras Tanura were hit in an exchange of fire, after a Houthi attack damaged an office tower in Riyadh and Saudi forces struck Hodeidah overnight Tuesday.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on a major crude loading terminal and a Red Sea port threaten liftings, raise war-risk premiums and can reroute crude and product tonnage away from the region.
storylines.latest: Reported today; Brent is $93.07, up 1.8%, which may partly reflect the strikes.
sources: Riyadh, Hodeidah and Ras Tanura Hit in Saudi-Houthi Exchange of Fire

storylines.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue, following tanker incidents near Oman, a mine strike east of Hormuz and a projectile hit on an outbound tanker. Tracking and identity obfuscation around the strait is also in question.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and mines raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
sources: Riyadh, Hodeidah and Ras Tanura Hit in Saudi-Houthi Exchange of Fire

storylines.title: Drone strikes on Russian-linked shipping beyond the Black Sea
storylines.what: The Russian RoRo Sparta II was struck by a suspected drone in the Baltic and drifted into Finnish waters. Ukrainian drone boats attacked Russian warships at the port of Benghazi in Libya.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes in the Baltic and the Mediterranean extend the war-risk zone for merchant shipping far beyond the Black Sea, with implications for insurance cover, routing and port calls.
storylines.latest: Libya's Tripoli-based government says it had no knowledge of the Benghazi drone boat attack, and Ukraine denies interfering in Libyan affairs.
sources: Ukraine Denies Interfering in Libyan Affairs After Benghazi Drone Strike

storylines.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
storylines.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January.
storylines.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment.
sources: Most Large Fuel Tankers Now Ship ‘Dirty’ Crude, Upending Trading

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations. The Russian Navy is reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean.
storylines.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties and vessel positions, and obfuscated signalling makes that verification harder.
sources: Webinar on-Demand Now: Seatrade Maritime News webinar tackles the rising threat of GPS/GNSS attacks on global shipping

storylines.title: IMO net-zero rules for LNG and alternative fuels
storylines.what: The IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee opens MEPC85 on 30 November without final rules on how LNG, bio-LNG and e-LNG carbon values are measured under the Net-Zero Framework.
storylines.why_it_matters: The accounting treatment of LNG determines the compliance economics of LNG-fuelled tonnage and newbuilding decisions, including LNG carrier and dual-fuel orders now being placed.
storylines.latest: No MEPC news today, but Bonny Gas Transport ordered two more LNG carriers at Hudong-Zhonghua and an LNG dual-fuel PCTC entered service for SUARDIAZ.

storylines.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations. The Russian Navy is reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean.
storylines.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties and vessel positions, and obfuscated signalling makes that verification harder.

storylines.title: IMO net-zero rules for LNG and alternative fuels
storylines.what: The IMO's Marine Environment Protection Committee opens MEPC85 on 30 November without final rules on how LNG, bio-LNG and e-LNG carbon values are measured under the Net-Zero Framework.
storylines.why_it_matters: The accounting treatment of LNG determines the compliance economics of LNG-fuelled tonnage and newbuilding decisions, including LNG carrier and dual-fuel orders now being placed.
storylines.latest: No MEPC news today, but Bonny Gas Transport ordered two more LNG carriers at Hudong-Zhonghua and an LNG dual-fuel PCTC entered service for SUARDIAZ.
